newsitem.title: GERMANY: German army mock killing scenes recall Nazi horror.
newsitem.headline: German army mock killing scenes recall Nazi horror.

text.p: A German newspaper published on Sunday the first harrowing pictures from an amateur videotape of soldiers staging mock executions and rapes of civilians during a break in training for a peacekeeping mission in former Yugoslavia.

In a scene ghoulishly reminiscent of Nazi war atrocities, a youthful recruit in a Bundeswehr uniform is shown aiming a pistol into the mouth of another recruit in an image published on the front page of Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

Another photograph in the country's best-selling Sunday newspaper shows a German soldier wearing battle fatigues pretending to rape another recruit acting as a woman civilian, who is later shown being marched to "her" execution by soldiers.

Other photos show enactments of "civilians" being tortured and hanging from trees, images which carried horrifying recollections for Germans of World War Two atrocities carried out by Hitler's armies.
Private network SAT-1 said on Friday it had the tape and would broadcast it on Monday evening.
The army said eight recruits on the film made at the Hammelburg training ground near Wuerzburg in April 1996 had since completed their service and were no longer in the army.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe condemned the "unbelievable behaviour" and vowed swift and severe punishments for those involved and responsible.

The Bundeswehr's probe was focusing on officers who faced reprimands for failing to report on the incident, which took place during a break in a training for soldiers preparing for a mission in former Yugoslavia.
Lieutenant General Helmut Willmann, the army's inspector and top officer, said the acts by "a handful of mentally disturbed individuals" could not besmirch the German army's good name.

"I am horrified by what happened at the Hammelburg training ground," Willmann said in a statement released by the Defence Ministry: "This is an aberration that unfairly harms the reputation of every soldier.

"It is out of line with the principles of our leadership and training," he added. "Our soldiers have won praise and recognition in and out of Germany for the exemplary deployment at home and in former Yugoslavia. This fact will not be wiped away by a handful of mentally disturbed individuals."
The pacificist Greens party criticised Willmann for trying to write off the incident as an aberration as officers knew of the tape for more than a year but said nothing about it.

Juergin Trittin, chairman of the Greens, said the incident was the latest of a series of unsettling incidents. Trittin said there had been 53 reported incidents of right-wing extremism in the army in 1995.

"Equipped with the mentality of their grandfathers, who took pictures of Wehrmach crimes, the German soldiers have now marched into former Yugoslavia where the grandsons entertain themselves by making videos of executions and terror on the civilians," Trittin said.
Wolfgang Schraut, commander of Jaeger Battalion 571 where the incident took place, said the recruits in the video were no longer in the army and could no longer be punished by the army.
"We will not be able to get our hands on them any more," Schraut said. "They were released from the army in an entirely normal fashion after completing their military service."
Schraut said he did not know of the existence of the videotape until Friday and had learned that it was shown "on occasion in small circles among the comrades".

Some 3,000 Germans are in the NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in Bosnia. Around 4,000 Germans took part in SFOR's predecessor, the peace Implementation Force (IFOR) but were stationed in nearby Croatia.
Ruehe said in a statement late on Friday there was no excuse for the macabre imitations of rape and execution.

"This unbelievable behaviour is to be completely deplored," Ruehe said. "An investigation was launched immediately. The participants and their superiors can count on most severe consequences and possibly legal action."
